question_text: Light from a sodium lamp ($\lambda = 590\text{ nm}$) is diffracted by a slit of width $d = 0.30\text{ mm}$. The distance from the slit to the screen is $D = 0.87\text{ m}$. The width of the central maximum will be
solution:
The linear width of the central maximum in single-slit diffraction is given by:
$$\beta_0 = \frac{2\lambda D}{d}$$
Substituting the given values:
$$\beta_0 = \frac{2 \times (590 \times 10^{-9}\text{ m}) \times 0.87\text{ m}}{0.30 \times 10^{-3}\text{ m}} = 3.422 \times 10^{-3}\text{ m} \approx 3.4\text{ mm}$$

question_text: A star is going away from the earth. Then it shows
solution: Due to the Doppler effect in light, when a celestial source moves away from the observer, its apparent wavelength increases towards the longer wavelength (red) region of the visible spectrum. This phenomenon is known as a red shift.

question_text: Two light sources are coherent when
options: Their frequencies are equal and their phase difference is constant
solution: Two light sources are said to be coherent if they emit light waves of the same frequency (or wavelength) with a zero or constant phase difference over time.

question_text: In a Young's double-slit experiment using monochromatic light, the fringe width is $4\text{ mm}$. Now the whole arrangement is dipped in water $\left(\mu = \frac{4}{3}\right)$. Then the fringe width will be now
solution:
The fringe width in a medium of refractive index $\mu$ is given by:
$$\beta' = \frac{\beta}{\mu}$$
Given $\beta = 4\text{ mm}$ and $\mu = \frac{4}{3}$:
$$\beta' = \frac{4}{4/3} = 3\text{ mm}$$

question_text: If the screen (in YDSE) is perpendicular to the $y$-axis (line joining the sources), i.e., placed in the $x\text{-}z$ plane, the fringes will be
solution: The locus of points having a constant path difference from two point sources is a hyperboloid of revolution with the line joining the sources as the axis of symmetry. A plane screen perpendicular to this axis intersects the surfaces of constant phase difference in concentric circles. Hence, the fringes are circular.

question_text: Two Nicol prisms are first crossed and then one of them is rotated through $60^\circ$. The percentage of incident light transmitted is
solution:
Let unpolarized light of intensity $I_0$ fall on the first Nicol prism. The transmitted intensity is $I_1 = \frac{I_0}{2}$.
Initially, the prisms are crossed (angle $= 90^\circ$). When one is rotated by $60^\circ$, the angle between their transmission axes becomes $\theta = 90^\circ - 60^\circ = 30^\circ$.
By Malus's Law, the final transmitted intensity is:
$$I = I_1 \cos^2(30^\circ) = \frac{I_0}{2} \left(\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}\right)^2 = \frac{3}{8} I_0 = 0.375 I_0$$
Thus, the percentage of incident light transmitted is $37.5\%$.
